normalization: Original full-corpus per-feature minmax, shared across Human and AI
authorship: Computationally assisted visual nominations, recorded for the researcher; not statements that the researcher personally inspected every panel.
formula_selection: Completed R02/R06/R07 local-mixture assessment and preserved-block geometry control. R02 recurs across five primary genres; R06 whole-configuration/coupling transfer qualifies in four with review exception, while its shape contrast has an email exception. R07 is partial and fails the common-support cross-genre rule. Independent confirmation is not established.

records.title: Paired entropy band with a separated third feature
records.observed: In AI reviews, character bigram and trigram entropy form two close, narrow traces, while content-word entropy sits below them and has a different pattern of downward departures. A common A/B window reveals several narrow AI C strands, retained after full-vector duplicates are collapsed. Human reviews occupy a broader, more diffuse three-feature configuration.
records.question: As the two character-entropy features vary together, how does the position and variation of content-word entropy change relative to their collective configuration? Is this relation more specific than three separately narrow feature ranges?
records.remains: A compact three-feature cloud alone does not identify conditional dependence. The exact third-feature rule, supported regions, exceptions and a faithful formula remain to be established.
records.capture_requirements: Represent the joint location, width and orientation of the A/B band and the conditional position and spread of C, including its visible strands. Preserve the AI/Human difference without independently ranking the classes. A single averaged line must not erase the strands. Window selection is not exact matching of A/B; multiple values of C at identical A/B have not been established.

genre_review.email: Clear candidate variant. B and C remain tightly organized while A varies across the band; the third-feature position is associated with the joint anchor configuration. This is a curved corridor plus an additional group, rather than the review's near-horizontal C strata.
genre_review.review: Clear candidate variant. The third feature is organized relative to positions along and across the two-anchor arrangement. Its visible strata cannot be summarized faithfully by one constant A/B-to-C gap or one global straight line.
genre_review.legal: Clear candidate variant; different branch geometry. The recurring object is the arrangement of C around a jointly branching anchor band. AI is not simply narrower in every projection: the AI branches can occupy a wider A range. M02 is a local variant of the same proposed cross-genre family, rather than an unrelated experiment.
genre_review.abstracts: Weaker, overlapping variant; branch contrast unresolved. There is partial visual support for more constrained third-feature organization, but the shared rising relation is conspicuous in both classes. A generic positive relationship is a baseline, not itself an AI/Human signature.
genre_review.articles: Clear candidate variant. The organized third-feature corridor recurs, with different location and curvature from review. Human C often approaches the character-entropy levels in the original traces; AI C is often lower, with upper departures. The role of the shared band matters more than a fixed C threshold.
genre_review.papers: Unresolved; sparse and different anchor support. This is an observed change of feature ordering and occupied region. With little common A/B support, the displayed class difference cannot establish the same conditional contrast found in the larger genres.

records.title: Branching entropy band with third-feature organization
records.observed: AI legal documents show more distinct strands in the rising character bigram/trigram entropy arrangement. Content-word entropy occupies different positions along and across those strands. The Human cloud is more diffuse, with overlap and related colour organization.
records.question: Is there a repeatable branching three-feature arrangement, and how does the third feature vary within each branch rather than only along a single averaged line?
records.remains: Branch membership is not assigned. A single camera view can hide overlapping strands. The pattern is nominated locally; identical branching across genres has not been established.
records.capture_requirements: Retain multiple strands and their third-feature organization. A formula that averages the strands into one centre line fails this target even if its global prediction error is small. Preserve overlap and ambiguous branch membership.

genre_review.email: Compact AI arrangement, but not the same legal branching pattern.

genre_review.articles: Both classes have curved rising configurations. The legal branch distinction is not established here.

records.title: Review syntax geometry with sentence-length position
records.observed: The original review plots show a broadly rising Human arc-length/depth cloud and a compact downward-turning AI configuration. The new three-axis view retains the document triples, but the full sentence-length range compresses their central C variation.
records.question: How is sentence length arranged along the differently oriented arc-length/depth configurations, and does it distinguish regions that the two anchor features alone leave overlapping?
records.remains: A class difference in the A/B projection is visible; that alone is not a discovered three-feature rule. A focused shared view must establish C's role before a triadic formula is selected.
records.capture_requirements: Capture direction changes and curvature of the joint syntax configuration together with C placement. Do not call a two-feature reversal a demonstrated third-feature interaction. Keep the original document tuples and outlying branches.

genre_review.email: Human triples spread widely around a dense main arrangement; AI is more concentrated. This is not the same review reversal.
genre_review.review: Primary orientation contrast. The third-feature relation requires a focused common zoom or alternative projection.
genre_review.legal: Broadly rising syntax configurations occur in both classes with different spreads and outliers; the review reversal is not repeated.
genre_review.abstracts: Both classes contain rising joint configurations, with broader Human coverage. No identical review reversal.
genre_review.articles: Both classes show rising triples. This is an explicit exception to a universal reversal claim.

records.title: Lexical curve versus separated review strands
records.observed: Human reviews occupy a broad rising entropy/RTTR arrangement. AI reviews form narrow, more separated strands or clusters. The new 3D view retains these strands and their sentence-length coordinates.
records.question: Does sentence length separate the strands or organize the relation within them, rather than merely accompany a two-feature lexical pattern?
records.remains: The third-feature rule is not yet sufficiently described. The prominent review configuration must not be assumed to recur unchanged in every genre.
records.capture_requirements: Preserve curved Human geometry and AI multiple-strand geometry. Include C only if its specific collective role is established. A single linear sum or global correlation would not describe the nominated shape.

genre_review.email: AI occupies a compact rising joint arrangement and Human has wider coverage and long-sentence outliers.
genre_review.legal: Both classes overlap in a broader cloud; no unchanged review template.

records.title: Four-feature syntax arrangement with two apparent bands
records.observed: On the original shared-scale traces, arc length and mean sentence length frequently occupy a lower corridor, while depth and sentence-length variability occupy higher positions. In AI reviews the lower corridor is narrow and the upper two traces have structured separation; Human traces have wider excursions and crossings. Their relative layout changes by genre.
records.question: Does sentence-length variability change in a recognizable way with the collective position and geometry of the arc/depth/mean-length configuration? Can the whole four-feature arrangement be distinguished from merely adding a fourth marginal feature?
records.remains: The full four-feature rule remains under description. Fourth-feature colours in the full-range 3D view are too compressed in some panels to establish a clear conditional rule.
records.capture_requirements: Represent both the three-axis syntax configuration and the placement and variation of D around it. Preserve changes in band separation and crossings. A fourth feature appended to a classifier is not itself evidence that a four-feature motif has been captured.

genre_review.email: The apparent upper depth/variability band and lower arc/length corridor occur in both classes; Human excursions are broader. Layout alone is not unique to AI.
genre_review.review: Narrow AI lower corridor with more structured upper placement; Human shows wider excursions. Fourth-feature rule still unresolved.
genre_review.legal: Both classes show broader overlapping upper traces and lower arc/length values. Exact review geometry changes.
genre_review.abstracts: Depth is visibly above variability for much of both traces; the four-feature layout differs from email and review.
genre_review.articles: Human depth and variability traces often approach and cross; AI has a narrower apparent upper band. Requires document-level confirmation of the full configuration.
genre_review.papers: AI variability is closer to the lower sentence-length corridor than in Human in this small panel. Descriptive only.

records.title: Sentence spread and tail containment in narrower central bands
records.observed: After narrowing mean/median rectangles, the joint IQR/maximum response retains a thin low AI ribbon in short reviews and a lower AI envelope in short articles. Middle email and abstract regions show partial tail containment with substantial overlap. The minimum length remains marker context. This is a recurring response-envelope lead, not uniformly smaller AI variability.
records.question: As mean and median sentence length form a band, do middle spread and extrema form a constrained envelope in one class, and does question usage occupy particular parts of that envelope?
records.remains: Short email overlaps heavily. Legal overlaps through all three central regions and has long-tail AI points. Review middle/long windows and several article/abstract long windows lack AI support. Papers are too sparse. Remaining anchor variation and sentence counts have not been exactly controlled.
records.capture_requirements: Represent the response envelope of IQR and maximum jointly around the mean/median region, including thin levels, Human fans, overlap and long-tail exceptions. Keep empty support visible. Do not replace the graph by a single global subtraction or maximum threshold.

genre_review.email: In the short narrow rectangle (69 Human / 243 AI), the IQR/maximum clouds substantially overlap. In the middle rectangle (16 / 84), Human includes higher maximum-length extension while AI has its own high-tail exceptions and broad overlap. The long rectangle has no AI points. A universal email containment statement is unsupported.
genre_review.review: The shared short rectangle (114 / 296) retains thin AI levels at low maximum length while IQR changes; Human fans into higher maxima. This is a clear local joint-response shape. The middle and long rectangles have no AI representatives, so they show occupancy differences rather than response comparisons.
genre_review.legal: The short, middle and long rectangles all contain both classes. Their IQR/maximum clouds overlap strongly and share a rising envelope, with Human upper-tail extension and some long-tail AI points. Legal is a material exception to a uniformly narrow low AI response.
genre_review.abstracts: The short rectangle is imbalanced (16 / 216) and overlaps considerably. In the middle rectangle (82 / 36), AI mainly occupies the lower IQR/maximum portion while Human extends upward and outward, with many shared points. The long rectangle has only one AI point and cannot establish a stable response shape.
genre_review.articles: The shared short rectangle (77 / 124) shows Human extending into a much higher joint IQR/maximum fan while AI occupies a lower envelope; there is overlap. The middle rectangle has only seven AI representatives and the long rectangle none. The short-region shape is the useful comparison here.
genre_review.papers: The short rectangle is empty, the middle contains only one AI point, and the long contains 2 Human / 8 AI. Their sparse spread is descriptive and does not establish recurring tail containment.

records.title: POS response along the same repetition branches
records.observed: Integer repeat maxima explain the visible normalized-frequency rays in both classes. After exposing recovered alphabetic word count and keeping the same maximum-bigram/maximum-trigram states, the POS-entropy response still differs in useful regions, especially legal and abstracts, and the (3,2) state in reviews and articles. Review AI also shows a genre-specific type-count plateau as word count increases. The branch identity itself is a measurement scaffold, not a discovery of AI-only rays.
records.question: As lexical bigram and trigram variety move together, do repeated phrases, POS entropy and lexical variety organize into different branches or bands?
records.remains: Email branch responses overlap substantially; review (2,1) overlaps around the rising Human curve and (3,1) has only nine AI representatives. Article (2,1) and (3,1) have very few Human representatives. Papers occupy none of the three frozen low-repeat states. Word counts are visible, not exactly matched, and the audit recovers counts from CSV redundancies rather than independently reading raw texts.
records.capture_requirements: Keep branch state, word-count position and POS response together. Preserve type-count saturation as a review-specific shape and avoid claiming it survives every genre. A future descriptor may follow a branch-dependent response curve with exceptions; no such descriptor was fitted in this pass.

genre_review.email: At the same repeat states the POS response rises with word count in both classes and overlaps heavily. AI often occupies a narrower lower portion, while Human has both higher and low-entropy exceptions. This is a weak conditional variant, not a clean class split.
genre_review.review: AI bigram/trigram type counts level off while total words increase; its POS response also remains in a narrow band. Within (2,1), AI overlaps the Human rising curve. Within (3,2), AI remains flatter and lower as Human extends upward with length. The (3,1) comparison is sparse on the AI side. These are specific response/branch shapes, not only smaller clouds.
genre_review.legal: Within (2,1), (3,1) and (3,2), useful overlapping word-count regions retain a lower AI POS-entropy cloud with overlap. The (2,1) state is best supported (76 Human / 179 AI). Both classes share the type-count/word-count scaffold. This retains the response lead after exposing the integer repetition explanation.
genre_review.abstracts: Within (2,1), AI occupies a lower POS-entropy layer across overlapping word counts (75 Human / 301 AI). The other states show a related lower AI response but have fewer AI points in (3,2). The type-count/length scaffold is shared. Remaining within-state count distributions are not identical.
genre_review.articles: Most Human and AI documents occupy different length/repetition regions. The (3,2) state provides a useful overlapping-count comparison (42 Human / 16 AI) with lower AI POS response. The (2,1) and (3,1) states have only 12 and 5 Human representatives, respectively, so the full-cloud difference cannot be treated as equally supported in every branch.
genre_review.papers: Full-count views show lower AI POS entropy over overlapping word-count ranges, but all three frozen repeat states are empty for both classes. The branch-conditioned finding is therefore unresolved for papers; the marginal full-context appearance cannot substitute for a missing branch comparison.

records.title: Modifier bands with a depth response
records.observed: Four-token sentence-length intervals retain a lower AI depth layer in articles and compact review knots within fixed adjective/amod regions. Legal retains some lower-AI-depth portions with considerable overlap. Abstracts have a weaker comparison than the broad 15–25 interval suggested because several cells lose one class; its upper-adjective 18–22 interval has a small shared comparison with overlap. Email largely overlaps. These are configurations with explicit support limits, not one uniformly displaced surface.
records.question: Do adjective/adjectival-modifier and adverb/adverbial-modifier bands form a repeatable collective allocation, with suffix and tree-depth responses?
records.remains: Adverb/advmod and anchor values still vary inside each region; advmod is exposed in area rather than exactly matched. A marginal depth shift, remaining sentence construction, prompt/source composition or segmentation may contribute. The necessary role of each inspected member has not been proved, nor is pure irreducibility required to retain a useful composite.
records.capture_requirements: Retain which adjective region is occupied, the position and thickness of the adverb/advmod band, and the depth layer or knots above it. Allow branches, depth spread and genre variants; do not force one sign for adverb use. LY remains context, with no demonstrated necessary contribution. Sentence-length and source/segmentation context must remain visible.

genre_review.email: Lower-adjective cells overlap heavily at 14–18 and 18–22 mean sentence length. The 22–26 lower cell has only two AI points. Middle cells have very few Human points (7, 5 and 2), and upper cells have none. Thin AI portions remain visible, but their comparison does not support a strong recurring email depth rule.
genre_review.review: The 14–18 interval retains thin AI knots/curved pieces in lower and middle adjective regions against a broader Human depth fan (24/68 and 23/71). The middle knot changes position relative to the lower one; the Human cloud includes both higher and lower depth extension. Most longer cells have no AI support. This is a supported local collective shape rather than evidence over the entire sentence-length range.
genre_review.legal: Lower-adjective 18–22 and 22–26 cells retain AI mainly in lower depth portions with substantial overlap (20/10 and 22/20). Middle regions also overlap heavily, especially 22–26. Upper regions have at most one Human point per cell. Legal supplies partial recurrence and real exceptions, not a clean class-separating layer.
genre_review.abstracts: The lower adjective region has no shared occupied length cell. Middle regions have only 3/10 at 14–18 and 5/2 at 18–22. Upper-adjective 18–22 has 12 Human / 8 AI and retains lower AI depth portions with overlap; 14–18 has only two Human and 22–26 only one AI. The broad-window depth appearance is partly supported by different within-window length occupancy; stronger abstract recurrence remains unresolved.
genre_review.articles: The 14–18 interval retains lower AI depth across overlapping adverb positions in both lower (31 Human/94 AI) and middle (17/58) adjective regions. The graph shows Human above most AI points with some overlap. Longer cells retain only 6/5 AI at 18–22 and one AI in each lower/middle 22–26 cell. The short shared interval is the strongest well-populated conditional example; it does not justify uniform separation at every length.
genre_review.papers: There are no Human points in any of the nine selected cells and only one AI point in each of two upper-adjective cells. There is no supported Human/AI comparison in these length ranges.

records.title: Suffix-conditioned lemma and auxiliary geometry
records.observed: The lemma ceiling is count-constrained and appears in both classes. Nevertheless, within the same fixed suffix rectangle and shared verb-count ranges, email, abstracts and articles retain a high-diversity/low-auxiliary AI region. Review thin auxiliary strands and lower-diversity branches also persist within shared verb-count ranges. Legal often has higher AI auxiliaries with overlapping diversity. Different overall verb counts alone do not explain every visible configuration.
records.remains: Verb-count intervals are not exact count matching, word count still varies (shown by marker area), and suffix values vary inside each region. Auxiliary ratio has a word-count denominator. Low auxiliary use or high lemma diversity may each make substantial marginal contributions. Source/prompt repetition remains unresolved, and no universal direction or six-member mechanism has been demonstrated.
records.capture_requirements: Keep the suffix-region context, bounded lemma ceiling, auxiliary response and review-specific thin strands. Inspect verb count and word/sentence-length support before designing a formula. Retain passive/depth as context until a recurring contribution is demonstrated.

genre_review.email: In the lower-ED rectangle, 15–24 verbs (27 Human/86 AI) and 25–39 (24/51) retain high-variety/low-auxiliary AI points and broader Human responses. The 10–14 interval has only nine Human points and 5–9 has no AI. Higher ED is sparse in every interval. The useful lower-ED configuration is not solely a small-verb-count ceiling.
genre_review.review: In lower ED, 15–24 verbs (35/66) retain thin AI auxiliary levels with overlap; 25–39 (16/44) retain lower AI lemma-diversity branches at near-constant auxiliary levels. Higher ED retains strands but has only four or five Human points in its more occupied intervals. Overall AI diversity falls as verb count grows, but the within-interval configurations remain different. This is a directional variant of the three-genre configuration, not support for its high-diversity sign.
genre_review.legal: Both ED regions contain useful shared verb-count ranges. Lemma diversity and ceilings overlap; AI often occupies higher auxiliary positions, especially higher ED at 15–24 and 25–39 verbs. This remains an explicit counterexample to a universal low-auxiliary AI rule after verb-count context is exposed.
genre_review.abstracts: Lower ED retains high-diversity/low-auxiliary AI points at 10–14 verbs (58/28), with only seven AI at 15–24. Higher ED provides better support: 10–14 has 19/86 and 15–24 has 25/96, retaining the low auxiliary strip and high diversity with overlap. The response persists within these fixed count ranges, although count distributions are not identical.
genre_review.articles: Lower ED retains the configuration at 15–24 verbs (14/33) and particularly 25–39 (32/160). Higher ED at 25–39 (14/26) also places AI lower in auxiliaries and relatively high in diversity. Other higher-ED intervals have very few Human points. This is the best shared-count article evidence, while the full corpus still has large class differences in document and verb counts.
genre_review.papers: All frozen 5–39-verb intervals are empty in both suffix regions. Full-context graphs have much higher verb counts and overlapping diversity with lower AI cases. These empty ranges cannot assess paper-genre recurrence.

records.next_visual_action: Freeze a graph-specific descriptor target preserving the observed layer, knots or strands and the complete exception/support ledger. Assess reconstruction before making a transfer or classification claim.
records.independence_claim: Assisted exploratory corpus-level configuration. Exact matching, necessary interaction order, source independence and classifier performance remain unestablished.
records.closed_study_disposition: Assessed in the completed branch/arrangement study; original observations and missed configurations retained.

research_aim: Discover recurring abstract collective interaction patterns that survive changes of genre, and craft augmented-feature formulas to capture those observed patterns.

cross_genre_families.title: Third-feature organization around a coupled entropy band
cross_genre_families.target: As the joint A/B anchor configuration changes, C occupies relatively organized curved, layered or branching loci in the AI examples, compared with more diffuse Human configurations. Recurrence concerns this organization of the complete tuple, with genre-dependent occupied regions and shapes; it does not require the same C level, constant gap, branch count or review curve.
cross_genre_families.classification: Qualitative assisted visual assessment. These categories are not test outcomes, accuracy estimates, a vote establishing invariance, or evidence that every point separates.
cross_genre_families.role_of_third_feature: C colour organizes parts of the A/B arrangement; moving C to a spatial axis exposes layers, curvature and width changes. Some contrasts are also visible in B/C alone. Irreducible three-way dependence, conditional causation and added classifier value have not been demonstrated.
cross_genre_families.formula_target: Preserve the joint anchor corridor and the organization, curvature, width and possible branches of C around it across the nominated genres. A capture that reproduces only marginal ranges, a mean gap or the review example is incomplete. A future common feature rule must evaluate an unknown tuple without its true class, without class-specific scaling, and without secretly choosing a different scoring equation for each test genre.

cross_genre_families.title: POS entropy relative to the joint character-entropy configuration
exceptions: Review has weak overlapping separation. Papers descriptive.

cross_genre_families.title: Punctuation allocation and logarithmic response-band geometry
exceptions: Articles reverse the first conditional descriptor ordering. Abstract log-band IQR is similar to Human. Papers descriptive.

cross_genre_families.title: Sentence spread and tail containment in narrower central bands
exceptions: Short email overlaps heavily. Legal overlaps through all three central regions and has long-tail AI points. Review middle/long windows and several article/abstract long windows lack AI support. Papers are too sparse. Remaining anchor variation and sentence counts have not been exactly controlled.

cross_genre_families.title: POS response along the same repetition branches
exceptions: Email branch responses overlap substantially; review (2,1) overlaps around the rising Human curve and (3,1) has only nine AI representatives. Article (2,1) and (3,1) have very few Human representatives. Papers occupy none of the three frozen low-repeat states. Word counts are visible, not exactly matched, and the audit recovers counts from CSV redundancies rather than independently reading raw texts.

cross_genre_families.title: Modifier bands with a depth response
exceptions: Adverb/advmod and anchor values still vary inside each region; advmod is exposed in area rather than exactly matched. A marginal depth shift, remaining sentence construction, prompt/source composition or segmentation may contribute. The necessary role of each inspected member has not been proved, nor is pure irreducibility required to retain a useful composite.
